journey.title: Keep the current date when the range ends on a closed day
journey.goal: Weekends are unavailable. Arrow navigation must skip disabled days within the configured min/max range. If no available date remains in that direction, preserve the current valid date. Never clamp onto a disabled boundary or commit a disabled date after the search limit. Preserve the other field and normal pointer selection.

functionalJourney.title: Available weekday selection preserves actual booking dates
functionalJourney.goal: Weekends are unavailable. Arrow navigation must skip disabled days within the configured min/max range. If no available date remains in that direction, preserve the current valid date. Never clamp onto a disabled boundary or commit a disabled date after the search limit. Preserve the other field and normal pointer selection.

plan.root_cause: The adjustDate method incorrectly clamps to minDate or maxDate even when those dates are disabled (e.g., weekends), causing arrow navigation to land on a disabled date instead of preserving the current valid date when no further valid date exists in that direction.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify adjustDate to search for a valid non-disabled date within the min/max range; if the search hits a boundary without finding a valid date, retain the original date rather than clamping to a disabled boundary.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will now skip disabled days and, when no weekday remains within the allowed range, will keep the current date, ensuring users cannot move onto a disabled date and preserving the invariant that only selectable dates are reachable via keyboard.
functional_risks: The change alters the behavior when date arithmetic would exceed the min/max bounds: instead of clamping to the boundary date (even if disabled), the original date is retained. This could affect edge cases where a large day increment is intended to reach the boundary, but such usage is unlikely for arrow-key navigation.

If minDate or maxDate is itself a valid (non-disabled) date and the search overshoots due to a large day increment, the new behavior will keep the original date rather than moving to the boundary, which might be perceived as less responsive. However, arrow-key adjustments are single-day steps, making this scenario improbable.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowRight from a Friday (2026-10-23) with maxDate 2026-10-24 (Saturday) leaves the pickup date unchanged at 2026-10-23.
Verify that pressing ArrowLeft from a Monday after minDate behaves symmetrically.
Confirm that when a valid date exists in the direction of navigation, the date changes accordingly (e.g., ArrowRight from a Thursday moves to Friday).
Ensure that month/year navigation via the calendar UI remains unaffected.
Confirm that manual date selection via mouse or direct input still respects min/max and disabled days.
